subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Should the Gateway reject prototype-bearing JSON as defense in depth without a demonstrated sink, or close this report after targeted tests prove the current protocol and handler paths cannot pollute prototypes?
rationale: The report identifies a sensitive input boundary but does not establish exploitability, while globally rejecting or rewriting reserved keys could alter opaque configuration and plugin payload contracts.

options.title: Audit then decide
options.body: Run focused connect and authenticated-request pollution tests, patch the canonical protocol boundary only if they expose an unsafe sink, and otherwise close with the negative proof.

options.title: Reject reserved keys globally
options.body: Treat any nested `__proto__`, `prototype`, or `constructor` key as an invalid Gateway frame, accepting the resulting compatibility restriction as defense in depth.

options.title: Close without further proof
options.body: Treat direct `JSON.parse()` plus schema validation as sufficient because the report provides no unsafe merge or assignment sink.

recommendation.title: Audit then decide
recommendation.body: Run focused connect and authenticated-request pollution tests, patch the canonical protocol boundary only if they expose an unsafe sink, and otherwise close with the negative proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work places this contributor closest to the Gateway authentication and security boundary implicated by the report.
